subagent_note: None dispatched: the round tests the mechanism directly and its own gate turns out to ask the wrong question.

my_decision_rule_was_mismatched.the_question: does pathway membership predict a drug's behaviour
my_decision_rule_was_mismatched.what_i_gated_on: whether a leave-one-out group mean beats the grand mean in mean squared error
my_decision_rule_was_mismatched.why_different: association and estimation are not the same thing; with about five drugs per pathway a leave-one-out mean is extremely noisy
my_decision_rule_was_mismatched.data_says: permutation p of 0.000 and a correlation of 0.44, so the association is real
my_decision_rule_was_mismatched.corrected_verdict: the grouping carries real behavioural signal, but a crude five-drug mean is too noisy to exploit it

why_this_explains_the_model_level_result.ridge_shrinks: ridge pools information across all keys and shrinks group effects, so the same grouping that fails as a raw mean becomes usable
why_this_explains_the_model_level_result.so: the prior is real; exploiting it requires shrinkage
why_this_explains_the_model_level_result.unexplained: the anchor-versus-library asymmetry is recorded but not decomposed

instances: R107 demanded four of five streams in every pool

the_fourth_gate_mismatch.new_standing_rule: before writing a gate, ask whether the statistic answers the question being asked, not only whether it is significant

limits: 111 drug instances, and a drug mean averages away cell-to-cell variation
21 levels with about five drugs each makes leave-one-out estimation inherently noisy
the permutation calibrates the R2 and not the MSE
retrospective; no mechanism, clinical or drug-choice claim; no meta-learning or RSI
next_gates: replace the crude mean with a shrinkage estimator, a random-effects or empirical-Bayes fit on pathway, and see whether the shrunk prediction beats the grand mean at the drug level
